Senses.Explanation: Qiannu's soul leaves her body. In Chan records this phrase is the title and shorthand of a public case built around Wuzu Fayan's question: Qiannu's soul departed—which one is real? Wumen preserves the question and warns against running about wildly in his comment. Fojian Huiqin repeatedly presses Cishou Huaishen with the case until the record says an obstruction opened. Fuyan Ya discusses it with a lay official and warns him not to fasten onto Qiannu. Xueguan Zhiyin keeps the case open through its own alternatives: whether she is karmic consciousness or mind-born, and whether one or two; his answer says there is no need to display form and shadow. Chaozong Tongren answers the real-one question with two strikes and a warning against eloping. Baishan Dekai answers a layperson's version with ‘where money was lost in the river, dredge in the river.’ The tale-name has become a compact, repeatedly interviewed case formula. The entry reports the questions and answers without selecting a real Qiannu for them.
Senses.Note: Six exact witnesses across five sources clear the floor; Wumen's headword-absent comment is contrast evidence. Question, heading, entering-interview topic, and verse-like answers all concern the same named public case. Qiannu is a literary figure invoked by the masters and is defined here only through that Zen deployment, not through an outside tale summary.

Occurrences.Kwic: 倩女離魂倩女離魂五祖問僧云。倩女離魂。那箇是真底。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuzu Fayan, in The Gateless Barrier (無門關), asks the defining public question under the repeated case heading: Qiannu's soul departed—which one is real?

Occurrences.Kwic: 無門曰。若向者裏悟得真底。便知出殼入殼。如宿旅舍。其或未然。切莫亂走。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wumen Huikai, in The Gateless Barrier (無門關), comments on the preceding case and warns against running about wildly; this continuation lacks the headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鑑舉倩女離魂話，反覆窮之，大豁疑礙。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fojian Huiqin, in the Jiatai-era Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), repeatedly presses Cishou Huaishen with the exact case until the biography reports that the obstruction opened.

Occurrences.Kwic: 嘗謁福嚴雅禪師，與論倩女離魂，話未終，雅曰：隨他去也。公曰：師意如何？雅曰：切忌向倩女處著到。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fuyan Ya, in the Jiatai-era Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), discusses the exact case with a lay official and warns him not to fasten onto Qiannu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：倩女離魂事若何？師曰：月淡花移影。曰：未審他是業識？是意生？師曰：風搖水作波。曰：畢竟是一個？是兩個？師曰：形影不須彰，便脫狐窠臼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xueguan Zhiyin, in the Continued Abridgment of the Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元續略), answers successive public questions about the case's event, karmic consciousness or mind-born status, and whether it is one or two.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：倩女離魂，那箇是真底？師便打，僧無語，師曰：會麼？僧擬議，師又打，曰：切忌私奔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chaozong Tongren, in the Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), answers the real-one question with two strikes and a warning against eloping.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一居士問：「倩女離魂，那個是真？」師曰：「河裏失錢河裏摝。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baishan Dekai, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baishan Kai of Shanxi (山西柏山楷禪師語錄), answers a layperson's question on which Qiannu is real with ‘where money was lost in the river, dredge in the river.’
